title: The steep road: deeds first, then faith?
translation: [The steep road is] freeing a neck, or feeding, on a day of hunger, an orphan of kin or a poor one in the dust; then being among those who believe and urge one another to patience and to mercy.
body: Faith comes after a **“then” (thumma)**. Later in time? The Shia Enlightening Commentary prefers **rank**: faith stands above even feeding the poor, though deeds can also lead to faith. **Ibn Kathir** hears “along with” the deeds. Isaiah’s true fast is such deeds; for the **Augsburg Confession** (XX), works cannot merit grace, and faith brings them forth.
question: Does “then” in 90:17 put faith after the deeds in time, or above them in rank?
source_label: Enlightening Commentary on Q 90:17 · Ibn Kathir · Augsburg Confession XX
